activity.notes: Antigonus II Gonatas secured the Macedonian throne around 277/276 BCE. Pyrrhus occupied much of Macedonia in 274 BCE, creating a real interruption in Antigonus's rule; ATLAS therefore records this as the first of two reign Activities. The Production canonical Polity identity is reused as Macedon (display: 마케도니아).

sources.title: Antigonus (2), 'Gonatas', c. 320-239 BCE — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary identifies Antigonus II Gonatas as king of Macedonia from about 277/276 BCE, notes Pyrrhus's occupation of Macedonia in 274 BCE, and the removal of that threat with Pyrrhus's death in 272 BCE.
